title: Improve dedicated autoscaler burst policies and utilization reporting
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets saw burst exhaustion during sustained short spikes which violated throughput guarantees for a subset of customers. This PR tightens the autoscaler burst policy, adds a token-bucket based burst allocator with per-fleet windows, and improves utilization reporting so SRE and customers can observe burst consumption and long tail behavior.

What this change does: 1) Introduces a configurable burst_window_seconds and burst_token_capacity per fleet; the autoscaler refills tokens at a rate proportional to committed throughput and priority tier. 2) Adds queue-aware throughput guarantees: queued requests are counted against the burst budget to prevent queue pumping during global congestion. 3) Emits new metrics (fleet_burst_tokens, fleet_burst_refill_rate, dedicated_utilization_1m/5m/15m) and dashboards. 4) Adds end-to-end unit and integration tests, stress tests for token exhaustion, and a canary rollout path for Dedicated control plane.

Implementation notes: - Token bucket lives in the fleet controller and is deterministic across restarts via persistence to the autoscaler state store. - Refill logic uses a smoothed committed_throughput metric with a 30s EWMA to avoid oscillation. - When tokens are insufficient, the request routing layer will optionally (configurable) fall back to compatible lower-cost model variants or enqueue based on the fleet policy. - Utilization reporting aggregates pod-level last_1m/5m/15m CPU and token consumption and exports a per-fleet utilization_percent metric to the observability backend.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc: Linear ENG-4321 contains details and perf targets. - [x] Unit tests for token logic. - [x] Integration tests for queue-aware guarantees. - [x] Dashboard updates and Grafana panels. - [x] Documentation: dedicated autoscaling config docs updated. - [x] Canary rollout plan with feature flag.

Related: ENG-4321, ENG-4399, SUP-7782. This should reduce observed burst-related throughput regressions and give better visibility into Dedicated fleet economics.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: The refill EWMA smoothing constant needs a unit test to show it avoids oscillation under varying load patterns.
Maya Chen (author): Added unit test and updated docs to explain the smoothing window; see commit c3d4e5f.
Sofia Ruiz: Can we make the fallback to lower-cost model variants opt-in per-customer? Concern about silent quality regressions.
Maya Chen (author): Yes, fallback is behind fleet-level policy and off by default. Updated config schema and docs.
Liam O'Connor: CI stress job flaps on low-memory nodes in k8s CI. Recommend adding resource requests to the job.
Maya Chen (author): Increased resources for stress job and re-ran; CI now stable.
release_notes: Improve Dedicated autoscaler burst handling: configurable per-fleet token-bucket burst windows, queue-aware throughput guarantees, new observability metrics (fleet_burst_tokens, dedicated_utilization_*), docs and dashboard updates.
notes_for_ops: Canary deployment scheduled for 2026-03-01 in us-west-2; feature flag dedicated_burst_toggle rolled out to 10% of fleets initially. Monitor fleet_burst_tokens and dedicated_utilization_15m for regressions.
canary_plan: Rollout 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% across 6 hours with automated rollback on error budget or latency increase >5%
testing_summary: Added unit tests for refill policy and integration tests for queue-aware guarantees. Ran 6-hour stress tests simulating repeated short spikes; observed <1% request failures and token refill within expected windows.
performance_impact: Small CPU increase (~2%) on fleet controller due to token accounting; expected net cost reduction from fewer emergency horizontal scale-ups.
